subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled session-memory filenames and `# Session` headers use `agents.defaults.userTimezone` instead of host or `TZ` local time?
rationale: Current main has two memory timestamp paths with different semantics, and changing the shipped session-memory filename convention is compatibility-sensitive for existing workspaces.

options.title: Adopt `userTimezone` for memory artifacts
options.body: Use the existing configured-timezone contract for session-memory filenames, fallback slugs, and headers so it matches auto-flush and the reporter's expectation.

options.title: Keep host-local session-memory
options.body: Document session-memory as host-local and leave this issue open only if a narrower docs correction or explicit maintainer decision is needed.

options.title: Add a dedicated memory timezone option
options.body: Create a new memory-specific config knob only if maintainers want memory artifacts to diverge from both host-local and `userTimezone`.

recommendation.title: Adopt `userTimezone` for memory artifacts
recommendation.body: Use the existing configured-timezone contract for session-memory filenames, fallback slugs, and headers so it matches auto-flush and the reporter's expectation.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the current shipped host-local session-memory behavior and is the clearest routing candidate for deciding whether to extend it to configured `userTimezone`.
